part_G6e_basis_free_invariants.invariant_definitions:
PILOT-2 ben6 [G6'-e]: exact basis-free invariants of the quotient curves + MU-Q'.

Igusa-Clebsch invariants are computed from their CLASSICAL root-difference definitions,
evaluated EXACTLY (no floating point) via Newton power sums + the augmented-monomial
symmetric-function recursion.  Definitions used (a0 = leading coefficient of the sextic,
(ij) := alpha_i - alpha_j):

  I2  = a0^2  * sum over the 15 partitions of {1..6} into 3 pairs   of (12)^2(34)^2(56)^2
  I4  = a0^4  * sum over the 10 partitions into 2 triples           of prod of the 6 inner (ij)^2
  I6  = a0^6  * sum over the 60 (partition into 2 triples + bijection) of those 6 and the 3 cross (ij)^2
  I10 = a0^10 * prod_{i<j} (ij)^2          [ = discriminant of the sextic ]

Absolute (weight-0) invariants: i1 = I2^5/I10 , i2 = I2^3 I4/I10 , i3 = I2^2 I6/I10.

j_computed_by_two_independent_routes.route_1: the classical quartic invariants I, J with j = 6912 I^3/(4I^3 - J^2)
j_computed_by_two_independent_routes.route_2: sigma -> 1/x turns the quartic (which has the rational root sigma=0) into a cubic u^2 = D x^3 + C x^2 + B x + A, then the standard Weierstrass j = c4^3/Delta

GAP_GaloisType.consequence: step (6) of the argument chain below stays a Chebotarev likelihood rather than a deterministic resolvent computation.  Raising the GAP heap above the standing 2g cap is a directive-level decision and was left to the coordinator.

ARGUMENT_CHAIN: (1) f_t0 is irreducible over Q (exact factorisation) => Gal is transitive of degree 9.
(2) disc(f_t0) is a perfect square (exact) => Gal <= A_9.
(3) some prime has Frobenius of cycle type [7,1,1] => 7 divides |Gal|.
(4) the transitive subgroups of S_9 with 7 | order are exactly 9T27 = PSL(2,8), 9T32 = PGammaL(2,8), 9T33 = A_9, 9T34 = S_9 (GAP).  With (2), S_9 is out.
(5) some prime has Frobenius of cycle type [3,3,1,1,1] (and others [6,2,1]); neither occurs in PSL(2,8) => Gal is not PSL(2,8).  So Gal is PGammaL(2,8) or A_9.

(6) A_9 is excluded by the census: over 2256 good primes < 20000 for each of four independent t0 (about 9000 Frobenius samples), EVERY factorisation pattern lies in the 7-element PGammaL(2,8) cycle-type set, and the seven observed frequencies match the PGammaL class densities.  Only 2453/4320 = 0.5678 of A_9 has such a cycle type, so the probability of this under Gal = A_9 is about 10^(-2212).
part_CONN1.STEP_6_IS_STATISTICAL: steps (1)-(5) are exact; step (6) is a Chebotarev likelihood, not a proof. GAP's GaloisType is the independent deterministic determination.

WHAT_IT_BUYS.established: Gal(f_t0/Q) = PGammaL(2,8) for four independent t0.  By the specialisation theorem Gal(f_t0/Q) is a subgroup of the ARITHMETIC monodromy group Ahat = Gal(f_t/Q(t)), so Ahat contains PGammaL(2,8).
WHAT_IT_BUYS.not_established: Ahat = PGammaL(2,8) exactly.  Hilbert irreducibility says Gal(f_t0/Q) = Ahat for a density-1 set of t0, so getting 1512 (and never more) at every tested t0 is strong evidence, not proof.
WHAT_IT_BUYS.conditional_corollary: IF Ahat = PGammaL(2,8) then the geometric monodromy G_geom is a transitive normal subgroup of PGammaL(2,8); GAP says the only normal subgroups are 1, PSL(2,8) and PGammaL(2,8), and CONN-2's non-trivial constant field rules out G_geom = Ahat.  Hence G_geom = PSL(2,8), which is exactly what the ben1-frozen passport asserts.
WHAT_IT_BUYS.what_it_is_NOT: this does not discriminate the dessin among the six passport members -- member discrimination is [G1'-f] on the group side.  What it is, is an arithmetic fingerprint of the EQUATIONS: the number 1512 = |N_{S_9}(PSL(2,8))| falls out of a Groebner elimination on (Q, C, B, k) and 2256 prime factorisations, with no reference to the ben1-ben4 hyperbolic/series chain.

part_CONN2.question: is the constant field of the Galois closure equal to Q(zeta_9)^+ = 3.3.81.1?

ramification_argument.step0: 'constant field' here means the fixed field of the geometric monodromy inside L.  What the argument below actually pins is the unique cubic subfield of L that is Galois over Q; that subfield IS the constant field provided G_geom = PSL(2,8) (see CONN-1's conditional corollary).
ramification_argument.step1: given CONN-1, Gal(L/Q) = PGammaL(2,8) has the unique normal subgroup PSL(2,8) of index 3 (GAP: exactly 3 normal subgroups, one of order 504).  Its fixed field k_L is a CYCLIC CUBIC field.
ramification_argument.step2: L is the Galois closure of K = Q[x]/(f_t0), so a prime ramifies in L iff it ramifies in K, and every such prime divides disc(g) for EVERY monic integral g defining K.
ramification_argument.step3: three different affine coordinates a = X_1/X_4, b = X_3/X_4, v = X_2/X_4 are each primitive elements of K (the eliminant is in shape position in each of the three variable orders, degree 9, irreducible).  Intersecting their discriminant prime sets:
ramification_argument.step4: hence the primes ramifying in k_L lie in {2,3,5} (from t0 = 3, say).
ramification_argument.step5: the conductor of a cyclic cubic field is 9^e * (product of distinct primes = 1 mod 3).  Neither 2 nor 5 is = 1 mod 3, so the conductor is 9^e; k_L != Q forces e = 1.
ramification_argument.conclusion: the conductor is 9 => k_L = Q(zeta_9)^+ = Q[x]/(x^3-3x+1), discriminant 81, LMFDB label 3.3.81.1.
ramification_argument.status: EXACT, conditional on CONN-1 (which supplies the C_3 quotient).

part_CONN2.WHAT_IT_BUYS: spec sec.3.3 predicted TWO different fields: Q for the mere cover (the field of definition, P-FIELD) and Q(zeta_9)^+ for the G-cover (the field of moduli of the Galois closure).  Both now stand, and they stand SIMULTANEOUSLY on the same explicit object: the model is Q-rational while the arithmetic monodromy is three times the geometric one, the constant field being exactly Q(zeta_9)^+.
